children: In the year to the end of September, adjusted operating profit rose 42% to £487.1m on revenue of £1.8bn, up 21% on the previous year. Organic revenue grew 15%, which was an improvement on the prior year’s 11% growth.

Diploma highlighted a continued "outstanding" performance from Peerless - which supplies the US and European aerospace industry with fastening products, including nuts and bolts - with strong, broad-based organic growth of around 10% across the rest of the portfolio.
Adjusted earnings per share were up 45% to 255.6p, the adjusted operating margin increased to 26.5% from 22.5% and the full-year dividend per share was lifted 5% to 65.4p.
Diploma said it expects another strong performance in FY27, ahead of its financial model. The group expects total revenue growth of 12%, organic revenue growth of 6% and an operating margin of 25.5%.
Chief executive Johnny Thomson said it had been "another great year for Diploma".

"The strength of our performance this year demonstrates our continuous focus on ambitious earnings growth - up 45% - delivered with disciplined returns - at 25% - adding to our long-term track record," he said.

"Our strong organic growth of 15% has been complemented by acquisitions, growing and strengthening our portfolio. Since the start of FY26, we have welcomed 16 new businesses to Diploma, adding £50m of annualised operating profit while maintaining our disciplined approach to returns.

"The new year has started with great momentum. We have a diversified portfolio, attractive end market exposures, a strong acquisition pipeline and brilliant teams. We’re confident in delivering another year of sustainable quality compounding."
At 0922 GMT, the shares were down 0.1% at 7,151.68p.
